title: Arm Calls for Rack-Level CPU Benchmarks for Agentic AI, Claims Twice AMD's Performance
key_facts: Arm said on 15 Oct it developed a new CPU benchmark framework for agentic AI, with support from Fujitsu, Meta and OpenAI.
Arm claims its AGI CPU delivered about twice the task throughput per rack of AMD's fifth-generation EPYC Turin 9755.
The measurements were made by analyst firm Signal65 at Arm's request.
The AGI CPU, unveiled in March, is Arm's first in-house server CPU, co-developed with Meta.
Agents call tools, fetch data and run code; GPUs run the model while CPUs manage tool calls, data and scheduling.
Meta is adopting the AGI CPU in its next-generation Yosemite YV5 server rack.
quote_evidence: Arm claimed its AGI CPU delivered approximately twice the task throughput per rack of AMD's fifth-generation EPYC Turin 9755 server CPU under the new framework.
The measurements were conducted by analyst firm Signal65 at Arm's request.
why_it_matters_hint: Arm wants its benchmark to become the yardstick for AI-agent server chips.
notes: Claim is Arm's; test commissioned by Arm.
